thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGER fired: High 5xx rate detected on inference-gateway (eu-west1 + us-east1) — PagerDuty INC-54219. 5xx% = 18.3% over last 2m, baseline 0.5%. Affected route: /v1/generate -> model-srv. Links: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/inference-gateway (errors), https://pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-54219

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC-54219 created and escalated to oncall. Respond to acknowledge.

devon (oncall): acked. I'm jumping in. any immediate customer hits? :eyes:

louise (support): getting several support alerts from AcmeCorp and DeltaApps. Both see 503s in the last 5m. I'll open a status note if we confirm broader impact.

sara (SRE): joining. I see 503s from inference-gateway and model-srv-3 returning timeouts. Checking kvcache and proxy timeouts.

mike (infra): autoscaler metrics show large pending queue — scale policy didn't kick until qps spiked. Possible retry storm from clients. I'm looking at LB connection counts.

ops-bot: Runbook hint: if 5xx due to backend timeouts -> check model-srv pod restarts, increase gateway replicas, enable fallback routing to smaller model. See runbook: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/5xx-inference

devon (oncall): running quick commands now:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-srv-3 --tail=200 | grep ERROR
```

(devon): model-srv-3 shows repeated "upstream read timeout" and high CPU. Pod restarts = 0 but latency spikes.

sara (SRE): grabbing recent logs:
```
2026-03-14T02:19:01Z inference-gateway ERROR 503 backend timeout model-srv-3 seq=512
2026-03-14T02:19:02Z model-srv-3 WARN kvcache-miss key=prefix_0
2026-03-14T02:19:04Z model-srv-3 ERROR slow-infer duration=4.2s
```

sara (SRE): looks like model-side slowdowns under large seq lengths. Also seeing continuous small-burst requests from a handful of IPs (likely retrying clients).

mike (infra): immediate mitigation steps I can run: 1) bump inference-gateway replicas 2) adjust LB keepalive and connection draining 3) enable canary routing to gpt-lite-quant for new requests in region. Which should I do first?

devon (oncall): do all in parallel, prioritize replicas + canary routing. I'll coordinate.

ops-bot: Command executed (as devon): `k scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas=18 -n inference` -> OK (rolling).

ops-bot: Command executed (as devon): `redwood-route set-fallback --region eu-west1 --from=model-srv --to=gpt-lite-quant --weight=30` -> OK.

louise (support): posting interim customer message: "We're investigating elevated errors for inference requests in EU and US regions. Engineering is actively mitigating; we'll update in 15 minutes." Want me to post?

devon (oncall): yes please. Add note about temporary degraded accuracy if we fallback to smaller model.

louise (support): posted status with mention of potential degraded outputs. :thumbsup:

sara (SRE): monitoring graphs — errors dropped from 18% -> 6% in eu-west1 after canary. us-east1 still ~9%. Active backpressure visible on model-srv-3 queue length.

mike (infra): kicked an emergency scale for model-srv pool (replicas + warmup) and increased pod resources for hot nodes. Executed: `k scale deploy model-srv --replicas=24 -n inference` and `kubectl patch hpa model-srv --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}' -n inference`

devon (oncall): also enabled short-term client-side retry suppression via ingress header rewrite to reduce retry storms (edge rule): `ingress set header Retry-After: 5`

incident-bot: Note: autopage will not close automatically. Please resolve and update incident.

sara (SRE): 5xx now 2.1% in eu-west1 and 3.4% in us-east1. Latency on model-srv has improved after added replicas. Looks stable for now.

mike (infra): I've seen a correlated increase in long-sequence requests from one internal partner—poked them to confirm no runaway evaluation jobs.

devon (oncall): good catch — @eng-team we throttled the partner's job for now.

louise (support): customers AcmeCorp & DeltaApps acknowledged the status update; AcmeCorp said they switched to fallback – seeing degraded generation but they can work with it short-term.

sara (SRE): recommended next steps: 1) keep canary at 30% for 20m, 2) run KV-cache warmup scripts to reduce cold misses, 3) create a postmortem ticket.

devon (oncall): doing KV warmup: `./tools/warm_cache.sh --region eu-west1 --model=model-srv --concurrency=10` started.

ops-bot: KV warmup started by devon, 1200 prefixes queued.

mike (infra): scaling stable, no more CPU saturation on nodes. Prometheus rule fired: model_saturation > 80% triggered an alert — we'll tune thresholds.

devon (oncall): handing off in 30m to sara. I'll leave the canary and monitors set. If errors creep back up above 5% re-escalate.

sara (SRE): I'll take night shift. devon please file the incident ticket and include timeline + mitigations.

devon (oncall): filing ticket now -> https://issues/redwood/INC-54219-postmortem — added logs, commands, and links to dashboards.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-54219 acknowledged by devon (oncall). Current status: mitigated -> monitoring.

louise (support): I'll follow up with affected customers with summary and ETA for postmortem.

devon (oncall): TL;DR: Cause = model-srv slowdowns under large-seq requests + retry storm; Immediate mitigations = scale gateway & model pool, enable fallback routing to gpt-lite-quant, suppress retries, warm KV cache. Impact: degraded availability for a subset of requests in eu-west1/us-east1 for ~15m; major customers saw 503s but now on fallback or recovering.

sara (SRE): I'll pick this up for a full postmortem. Leaving monitors to watch for 1 hour then close. :wave:
